assertion.objects: Smooth E-representations of GL2(Q5); normalized principal series; full center acts by fixed zeta on extensions.

assertion.hypotheses: Smooth discrete action; same prescribed central character on entire middle term; finite coefficient extensions allowed.
assertion.conclusion: Principal-series smooth self-extension dimension equals one.
assertion.uniformity: Every such distinct-character principal series, including every point in the selected generic set.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Coincident inducing characters excluded; no supercuspidal or special-series claim.
assertion.normalization: I uses delta^(1/2), r uses delta^(-1/2), G acts by right translations; normalized induction characters are compared.
assertion.dependency_scope: Exact Jacquet coinvariants, exact induction/adjunction, explicit Bruhat two-cell computation, abelian extension calculation, all proved in Section1.
assertion.translation: At selected distinct-root nonexceptional crystalline points, apply to the smooth factor in BM4.19; BM4.11 and universal-completion/Galois bounds remain separate.

comparisons.needed: Smooth E-representations of GL2(Q5); normalized principal series; full center acts by fixed zeta on extensions.
comparisons.provided: The proof defines G, B, T, N and the category in which the full center acts as zeta on every middle term. This is the smooth Ext category appearing in BM4.19, before tensoring the algebraic factor.

comparisons.needed: E a finite extension of Q5 containing square root5; chi != w chi; selected consumer also requires irreducible principal series.
comparisons.provided: The two inducing characters differ on T; the consumer removes repeated Frobenius roots. Finite coefficient extension supplies delta^(1/2) and does not change the direct one-dimensional calculation.

comparisons.needed: Smooth discrete action; same prescribed central character on entire middle term; finite coefficient extensions allowed.
comparisons.provided: Exact Jacquet coinvariants and normalized induction are proved for smooth discrete E-actions. Compact averaging is used only in characteristic zero.

comparisons.needed: Principal-series smooth self-extension dimension equals one.
comparisons.provided: Derived adjunction and the two Bruhat constituents reduce Ext1 to the self-extension of chi plus the cross-extension. The cross-extension splits; the self-extension is determined by c(5).

comparisons.needed: Every such distinct-character principal series, including every point in the selected generic set.
comparisons.provided: The proof does not depend on a chosen conductor, eigenvalue magnitude or filtration. Every distinct pair has a separating T-element and the same valuation computation.

comparisons.needed: Coincident inducing characters excluded; no supercuspidal or special-series claim.
comparisons.provided: If chi equals w chi, the separating-element splitting fails; those points are explicitly excluded. No conclusion uses a supercuspidal or Steinberg extension theorem.

comparisons.needed: I uses delta^(1/2), r uses delta^(-1/2), G acts by right translations; normalized induction characters are compared.
comparisons.provided: The open-cell integral contributes |a/d|, cancelling the induction and Jacquet half-modulus factors. Its remaining character is w chi; the closed cell gives chi.

comparisons.needed: Exact Jacquet coinvariants, exact induction/adjunction, explicit Bruhat two-cell computation, abelian extension calculation, all proved in Section1.
comparisons.provided: The proof supplies exactness, the adjunction, enough injectives, the two-cell calculation and the abelian extension computation. It retains BM4.11 for removing the algebraic factor and the earlier universal-completion argument.

comparisons.needed: At selected distinct-root nonexceptional crystalline points, apply to the smooth factor in BM4.19; BM4.11 and universal-completion/Galois bounds remain separate.

applications.available: Direct idempotent-lifting and compact-Nakayama proof over the fixed-central-character completed group algebra.
applications.needed: Final integral projective-cover inference in BM5.2 after its snake-lemma calculation.

assertion.statement: An O-torsion-free compact R-module with finite projective reduction is finite projective; a reduction projective cover gives the corresponding integral cover.
assertion.objects: R=O[[K]] modulo z-eta(z) for the compact central character eta; compact profinite modules and continuous maps.
assertion.parameter_range: O coefficient DVR; K=GL2(Z5); prescribed integral central character.
assertion.hypotheses: R pi-adically complete; M O-torsion-free; M/piM finite projective; essential reduction epimorphism for cover conclusion.
assertion.conclusion: M is finite projective and its lifted epimorphism is a projective cover.
assertion.uniformity: Every module satisfying these hypotheses; no uniformizer-character condition needed.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No conclusion if O-torsion-freeness or projective reduction is omitted.
assertion.normalization: pi is the coefficient uniformizer. For actual Coker(x), eta=zeta_BM^(-1) under Pontryagin duality; Section1 zeta is a smooth-side character.
assertion.dependency_scope: Idempotent polynomial iteration, projectivity, Tor vanishing and compact Nakayama are proved in Section2.
assertion.translation: BM5.2 supplies M=Coker(x), torsion-freeness and the reduction cover. Finite target generators lift to a compact closed image surjecting the target; essentiality makes that image the full cover, and projectivity splits it, establishing finite projectivity.

comparisons.needed: R=O[[K]] modulo z-eta(z) for the compact central character eta; compact profinite modules and continuous maps.
comparisons.provided: Section2 separates compact eta from smooth zeta and defines the quotient using z-eta(z). BM Pontryagin duality makes eta the inverse of its smooth central character.

comparisons.needed: O coefficient DVR; K=GL2(Z5); prescribed integral central character.
comparisons.provided: The iterative idempotent correction is a polynomial in one matrix, so it works in noncommutative matrix rings over the pi-complete R. No commutativity of K is assumed.

comparisons.needed: R pi-adically complete; M O-torsion-free; M/piM finite projective; essential reduction epimorphism for cover conclusion.
comparisons.provided: The finite projective reduction yields an idempotent and a finite projective lift P. O-torsion-freeness of M removes Tor1 when reducing the kernel sequence.

comparisons.needed: M is finite projective and its lifted epimorphism is a projective cover.
comparisons.provided: The lift P to M is surjective by compact Nakayama and injective by the reduced kernel calculation, hence is an isomorphism. Essentiality of the reduction epimorphism then lifts by applying Nakayama to M/L.

comparisons.needed: Every module satisfying these hypotheses; no uniformizer-character condition needed.
comparisons.provided: The calculation is independent of the rank of the finite projective reduction and of the central character, provided the specified compact quotient ring and torsion-freeness hypotheses hold.

comparisons.needed: No conclusion if O-torsion-freeness or projective reduction is omitted.
comparisons.provided: Without torsion-freeness the kernel reduction need not be zero. Without finite projective reduction there is no finite idempotent lift. Neither excluded situation occurs after the cited BM snake-lemma calculation.

comparisons.needed: pi is the coefficient uniformizer. For actual Coker(x), eta=zeta_BM^(-1) under Pontryagin duality; Section1 zeta is a smooth-side character.
comparisons.provided: The coefficient uniformizer pi is distinct from the group scalar5; all compact modules use eta=zeta_BM^(-1), so their maps remain in the actual BM category.

comparisons.needed: Idempotent polynomial iteration, projectivity, Tor vanishing and compact Nakayama are proved in Section2.
comparisons.provided: The new proof supplies only integral projectivity and cover essentiality. It does not construct the K-injective enlargement, the endomorphism x or its reduction exact sequence.

comparisons.needed: BM5.2 supplies M=Coker(x), torsion-freeness and the reduction cover. Finite target generators lift to a compact closed image surjecting the target; essentiality makes that image the full cover, and projectivity splits it, establishing finite projectivity.
comparisons.provided: BM reduction is a projective cover of a finite semisimple target. Lift its finite generators; compactness gives closed image, essentiality gives surjectivity, and projectivity splits. The lemma then applies to Coker(x).
